This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Hi-hat: eighth notes**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read the band's last four bars on the staff underneath. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Drum grooves](index.qmd#drums)

## The pattern

Closed hi-hat on every eighth note, all of one weight, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The basic rock beat. In 3/4: six eighths, kick on 1, snare on 3.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock*, *Piano ballad*, *Acoustic strum*, *Dance pop* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Hi-hat: quarter notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The first rock beat. In 3/4: hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums-hhquarters.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: quarter notes","opts":{"groove":"hhquarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Hi-hat: eighth notes, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The hi-hat now on every eighth, all one weight. Kick and snare stay where they were. Keep the hand going while the kick and snare join it.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}},{"label":"Hi-hat: quarter notes (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"hhquarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>
